# Draft:Business of Software Conference

Business of Software Conferences
Business of Software (BoS) is a conference and global community for software founders, entrepreneurs and leaders. Founded in 2007, BoS organizes in-person events (in Europe and the USA), publishes hundreds of talks and resources, and supports a community of software companies focused on building sustainable, profitable and people-centric products and organisations.
History & Mission
* BoS was started by Neil Davidson (co-founder of Redgate Software) who felt that most conferences at the time emphasized either coding or funding/selling software businesses, but neglected the core challenges of building and growing sustainable software companies.
* The first BoS events launched in 2007. Over time, it expanded into both European and U.S. editions.
* According to BoS, the aim is to create a space “somewhere between a land where teenagers on skateboards sell their startups to Google and a land where everyone works for Microsoft.” In other words: not hype-focused, not corporate-factory, but grounded, human, and sustainable.
* The community around BoS is global and believes in “building companies people love and products people love using.”
Format & Approach
* BoS is described as a single-track, intimate, multi-day conference aimed at founders, CEOs, product-team leaders and other decision makers in software companies. Talks cover topics beyond coding or fundraising: leadership, product strategy, marketing, pricing, hiring, culture, JTBD, mental health and more.
* Attendance is intentionally capped to maintain a small, collaborative environment. BoS emphasizes vulnerability, open discussion, and peer learning over flashy keynotes or sales pitches.
* There are no vendor booths or sponsor “sales talks.” Instead, every talk is curated, speaker-led and focused on sharing real lessons from experienced practitioners.
* Networking and community building are central: participants often cite the “hallway track,” shared meals, round-table discussions, and informal chats as among the most valuable aspects of the conference.
Activities & Offerings
* Conferences: BoS runs events in both Europe (e.g., BoS Europe) and the USA (BoS USA), typically twice per year. Locations have included Cambridge, UK (for Europe) and Raleigh, NC (for the USA).
* Talk Library: As of now, BoS’s official site notes over 400 talks spanning roughly 17 years of conferences. Topics include product-market fit, pricing, strategy, leadership, company culture, customer research, and more.
* Free Resources: In addition to recorded talks, BoS offers guides, templates, and frameworks, e.g., pricing guides, product-management resources, and the popular “[https://businessofsoftware.org/playlists/jobs-to-be-done/playlist/ Jobs To Be Done] (JTBD)” materials.
* Community & Ongoing Engagement: BoS positions itself not just as an event organizer, but as a community. It offers periodic updates, newsletters, and opportunities to connect founders, leaders, and teams globally.
Values & Philosophy
The BoS community operates under a set of core principles:
* Quality over size: Rather than chasing large-scale growth, BoS limits attendance and prioritizes depth, reflection, and meaningful conversation.
* Question the status quo: BoS encourages founders and leaders to challenge conventional wisdom, whether in product development, growth strategy, pricing, or culture.
* Transparency, openness, and humility: Participants are encouraged to share struggles, mistakes, and real-world lessons, not just success stories or hype.
* Expert-led, practitioner-driven content: Speakers and talks are chosen for real-world experience and relevance, not based on sponsorship or publicity value.
* Long-term thinking: BoS targets sustainable business building, treating software companies as long-term projects, not quick exits or short-term growth hacks.
Notable Speakers & Endorsements
Over the years, BoS has featured talks from respected entrepreneurs, founders, and product leaders. Some individuals publicly associated with high regard for BoS include:
* [https://businessofsoftware.org/talks/speakers/dharmesh-shah/ Dharmesh Shah] (Founder of HubSpot), described BoS as “the only place I’ve found honest conversations about building software businesses.”
* Carl Ryden (Founder of PrecisionLender) — cited BoS as instrumental in the company’s growth (sold for US$510 million).
* Scott Farquhar (Co-founder & CEO, Atlassian) — said that BoS is “the only place I feel, professionally, among my peers.”
(BoS publishes many testimonials like these on its website.)
Significance & Impact
BoS occupies a distinctive niche among conferences and professional gatherings in the software/SaaS world:
* Focus beyond code or fundraising: Instead of emphasizing technical skills or capital-raising, BoS centers on the human, cultural, strategic, and organisational challenges of building sustainable software companies.
* A global, supportive community: By limiting conference size and emphasising honest, open dialogue, BoS fosters trust and peer-to-peer learning among founders and leaders.
* Practical, long-term thinking: The materials (talks, guides, frameworks) are grounded in real-world experience and designed to help teams navigate growth, product-market fit, pricing, organisational scaling, and sustainable business decisions.
* Longevity: With more than a decade of consistent activity, and hundreds of talks and resources, BoS has built a legacy that goes beyond a one-off event or trend.
